title: Why You Shouldn't Look Out the Window After a Nuclear Flash
description: A nuclear bomb goes off fifteen miles away, and the deadliest move is walking to the window. Two real rules decide your night, then the wind turns. Would you stay in the basement or drive out?

scenes.narration: Imagine you see a nuclear flash fifteen miles away, and what injures most people that far out isn't the heat. It's window glass.
The sky turns white, brighter than noon. Then... nothing. No sound. Total silence.
Rule one: get down, away from glass. You see, the blast wave travels like thunder after lightning. Fifteen miles out, it reaches you over a minute after the flash.
Forty seconds. You want to stand up and look. Sixty seconds. You stay flat.
Then it hits. The ground shakes, and a roar rolls over the city like a passing train.
Your car is right there. [pause] You run past it, into the building.
Rule two: get inside and stay inside for twenty-four hours. You see, fallout is radioactive dust falling like invisible snow, and every wall between you and it is a shield.
You turn on the radio. The dust gets weaker fast. After seven hours it's ten times weaker. After two days, a hundred.
One hour in. Your phone? No signal.
Then the radio says the wind has turned. The cloud is drifting straight toward you, and your car is outside.
Do you stay in the basement, or drive out before the dust lands? Comment A or B.
